ai.definition: Collaborative Swarm Logic is a software technology that enables thousands of small robots to operate as a single cohesive unit through decentralized control systems.
ai.howItWorks: This system utilizes stigmergy and bio-inspired algorithms such as ant colony optimization to facilitate emergent behavior among the swarm. Each robot in the swarm communicates with its neighbors, leaving 'traces' or signals that influence other robots, leading to coordinated actions without centralized command.
ai.problemSolved: It addresses the challenge of coordinating large numbers of autonomous robots for complex tasks where a central control system would be impractical due to scale and complexity.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves creating lightweight, low-power consuming robots capable of repeated communication. The process includes designing compact electronics, durable yet flexible materials, and efficient power management systems.
ai.buildProcess: The build process begins with component design, followed by assembly using automated machinery for precision. Testing focuses on individual robot performance and swarm coordination through simulated environments before real-world deployment.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the development of robust communication protocols, miniaturization technology, and energy-efficient hardware designs to accommodate thousands of robots in a single system.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as the technology matures and more applications are identified. However, challenges remain in scaling up production and ensuring reliability across large swarms.
ai.regulation: Current regulations vary widely by country but generally fall under guidelines for unmanned systems and autonomous technologies. Specific frameworks will likely emerge as the technology advances.
ai.risks: Technical risks include ensuring robustness against interference and maintaining swarm coordination over long distances. Non-technical risks involve ethical considerations, security threats, and potential misuse of such systems.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain but could be significant in sectors like logistics and search-and-rescue operations where efficiency gains can lead to substantial cost savings.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on enhancing communication protocols, increasing the number of robots that can operate effectively as a swarm, and integrating more advanced AI for better decision-making capabilities.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking. Power consumption scales with the size of the swarm but remains manageable through efficient design.

glossary.def: A mechanism of indirect communication wherein the environment is used as a medium for storing and reading information.
A bio-inspired algorithm that models the foraging behavior of ants to solve optimization problems, often used in swarm robotics for pathfinding and task allocation.

subsystems.name: Communication mesh
subsystems.role: lets robots share state and coordinate without a central hub.

subsystems.name: Local perception
subsystems.role: each robot senses its immediate surroundings and nearby neighbours.

subsystems.name: Decentralized decision engine
subsystems.role: simple local rules produce complex group behaviour.

subsystems.name: Task allocation
subsystems.role: assigns jobs to robots dynamically as conditions change.

subsystems.name: Simulation and validation
subsystems.role: tests swarm algorithms before any hardware is deployed.

subsystems.name: Operator interface
subsystems.role: gives humans high-level command and oversight.

buildSteps.title: Define the mission
buildSteps.detail: Specify the tasks (e.g. search and rescue), the environment, robot capabilities and communication range.

buildSteps.title: Design local interaction rules
buildSteps.detail: Choose algorithms such as stigmergy and ant colony optimization that will produce the desired emergent behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Build a simulation
buildSteps.detail: Implement the rules in a multi-agent simulator with realistic sensing and communication models.

buildSteps.title: Evolve and tune
buildSteps.detail: Use evolutionary algorithms or reinforcement learning to optimise parameters for the mission.

buildSteps.title: Port to physical robots
buildSteps.detail: Integrate the algorithms with robot middleware such as ROS 2, and connect to sensors and actuators.

buildSteps.title: Test with small groups
buildSteps.detail: Run experiments with tens of robots in controlled indoor or outdoor arenas.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Address communication bottlenecks, localisation drift and robustness to individual failures.

buildSteps.title: Deploy in the field
buildSteps.detail: Integrate with logistics or search-and-rescue operations, with human operators supervising at a high level.

prerequisites.why: mesh radios exist, but scaling to thousands of nodes with low latency and high reliability is not yet routine.
microcontrollers and systems-on-chip are capable of running swarm algorithms on small robots.
cameras, LiDAR and proximity sensors are small and cheap enough for large numbers of robots.
many algorithms are published, but few have been proven with thousands of physical robots.
multi-agent simulators allow rapid iteration before hardware is built.
no standards exist for certifying large, self-organising robot fleets in public spaces.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes and limited pilots with tens to hundreds of robots
pathway.unlocks: proof of basic coordination in warehouses, agriculture and drone light shows.

pathway.milestone: fully decentralized swarms of hundreds in logistics and agriculture
pathway.unlocks: flexible automation that adapts to changing tasks without a central controller.

pathway.milestone: swarms of thousands for search and rescue and environmental monitoring
pathway.unlocks: rapid area coverage and resilient operation after disasters.

pathway.milestone: heterogeneous swarms mixing air, ground and water robots
pathway.unlocks: complex missions that self-organise with minimal human intervention.
